name: single_chunk_doc

input.text: Bats fly at night. They eat insects. Some bats live in caves.

chunks.text: Bats fly at night. They eat insects. Some bats live in caves.

why: spec/chunking.md rule 5: a doc that fits under the budget entirely is exactly one chunk, even though it has several sentences.

name: three_chunk_doc_built_from_corpus_style_text

input.text: Alice paid Bob five dollars. Bob bought a sandwich with it. Carla watched them both. Dev arrived late to the shop. The shop closed at noon that day. Everyone went home after that. It was a quiet afternoon in town. Nothing else happened worth noting.

chunks.text: Alice paid Bob five dollars. Bob bought a sandwich with it. Carla watched them both.
Dev arrived late to the shop. The shop closed at noon that day. Everyone went home after that.
It was a quiet afternoon in town. Nothing else happened worth noting.

why: 8 sentences (relational/negation prose in the style of spec/eval/corpus/005.txt) pack into exactly 3 chunks under a 25-token budget, each chunk ending on a sentence boundary.

name: chunk_boundaries_never_split_a_sentence

input.text: Alice paid Bob five dollars. Bob bought a sandwich with it. Carla watched them both. Dev arrived late to the shop. The shop closed at noon that day. Everyone went home after that. It was a quiet afternoon in town. Nothing else happened worth noting.

chunks.text: Alice paid Bob five dollars. Bob bought a sandwich with it.
Carla watched them both. Dev arrived late to the shop.
The shop closed at noon that day.
Everyone went home after that.
It was a quiet afternoon in town.
Nothing else happened worth noting.

why: a tighter budget on the same doc produces more chunks, but every chunk still starts and ends exactly on a sentence boundary -- no chunk ever contains a sentence fragment.

name: oversized_sentence_pre_split_by_tts_safe_rule

input.text: This sentence is somewhat long and uses several words to fill space nicely. Short one here. This next sentence is also fairly long and uses several words to fill space nicely too.

chunks.text: This sentence is somewhat long and uses several words to fill
space nicely. Short one here.
This next sentence is also fairly long and uses several words
to fill space nicely too.

why: spec/chunking.md rule 2: the first and third sentences each individually exceed the 15-token budget, so each is pre-split at word boundaries (the same rule split.ts uses) before packing; the leftover tail of a split sentence still packs normally with the next real sentence.

name: two_sentences_each_individually_oversized_both_pre_split

input.text: Alice paid Bob five dollars today. Bob bought a sandwich with it later on.

chunks.text: Alice paid Bob five
dollars today.
Bob bought a sandwich
with it later on.

why: with a very small budget both sentences need pre-splitting; each sentence's pieces still tile that sentence's own span, and a leftover piece with nothing left to merge with becomes its own chunk.

name: exactly_at_budget_stays_one_chunk

input.text: Alice paid Bob five dollars today.

chunks.text: Alice paid Bob five dollars today.

why: the budget check is <=, not <: a doc whose token count exactly equals chunk_input_tokens is still a single chunk, not split.

name: max_chunks_exactly_at_cap_is_fine

input.text: One sentence. Two sentence. Three sentence.

chunks.text: One sentence.
Two sentence.
Three sentence.

why: exactly max_chunks chunks is allowed; the cap only rejects going OVER it.

name: over_limit_input_refused

input.text: One sentence. Two sentence. Three sentence. Four sentence. Five sentence.

why: spec/chunking.md's max_chunks rule: 5 sentences need 5 chunks under this budget, which is over the max_chunks cap of 2, so chunkSentences refuses with input_limit and reports how many chunks it would have needed.

name: one_more_than_the_cap_also_refused

input.text: One sentence. Two sentence. Three sentence.

why: the same doc as max_chunks_exactly_at_cap_is_fine, but with the cap one lower, now fails -- confirms the boundary is exact.
